name: Telescope Array (Utah)

intervals.label: operations
intervals.quote: 16 years of data collected from 11 May 2008 to 10 May 2024
intervals.note: The 10 May 2024 date is the end of a 16-year analysis dataset window used in a 2026 paper, not a stated end of operations; no fetched source says the array has stopped taking data.

area.quote: covering an area of about 700 km^2

altitude.quote: at an altitude of approximately 1400 m above sea level

summary.plain: A cosmic-ray observatory in the Utah desert, near Delta: 507 detector stations spread across about 700 square kilometres, watched by three telescope stations, to catch the rarest and most energetic particles from space.
summary.technical: Hybrid ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observatory near Delta, Utah, USA, at about 1400 m altitude, comprising a 507-counter surface-detector array over ~700 km^2 and three fluorescence-detector stations; operating since 11 May 2008 and extended since 2019 by the four-times-larger TAx4 array.
